  R28 NEW BLOCK — 'LEADING CANONICAL WORKED EXAMPLE — My dbt incremental model with incremental_strategy=merge used to run in 5 min, now runs in 40 min — same SQL, same row volume. What changed?'
  - Diagnosis-pattern-in-one-sentence: each MERGE INTO produces one position-delete file per affected data file on Iceberg v2 MoR; without periodic compaction, MERGE plan-time slows linearly with delete-file count. Confirmed by trinodb/trino issue #17114.
  - Step 1 diagnostic SQL — content-code-grouped query against `\"fct_events$files\"` showing DATA / POSITION_DELETES / EQUALITY_DELETES file_count + total_mb + avg_kb + min/max_kb. Iceberg manifest spec codes (0 / 1 / 2) verified at iceberg.apache.org/spec/.
  - Interpretation table mapping diagnostic-output patterns to verdicts (4 rows: delete-file-dominant, tiny-delete-files, compounding data-file fragmentation, delete-files-near-zero-so-investigate-elsewhere).
  - Step 2 confirmation SQL — `\"fct_events$snapshots\"` grouped by date_trunc('day') and operation column to show 30-day MERGE traffic (operation='replace' for row-level update commits).
  - Step 3 fix-on-the-production-stack: ORDERED three-step recipe — (1) Spark `CALL iceberg.system.rewrite_position_delete_files(table => 'analytics.fct_events')` to compact delete files (NO Trino equivalent on 467), (2) Trino `ALTER TABLE iceberg.analytics.fct_events EXECUTE optimize(file_size_threshold => '128MB')` to compact data files, (3) Trino `EXECUTE expire_snapshots(retention_threshold => '7d')` to release MinIO bytes. Ordering rationale explicit.
  - Step 4 prevention-at-dbt-model-level: 3 levers (narrow merge_update_columns, partition-aligned MERGE join predicate, copy-on-write switch with explicit write-amplification caveat).

  R28 NEW DO-NOT-WRITE TABLE (10 rows): bans (i) `ALTER TABLE fct_events EXECUTE rewrite_position_delete_files` (no such Trino procedure on 467; Spark-only); (ii) `EXECUTE optimize(rewrite_deletes => true)` (no such param; Trino's optimize has ONE param `file_size_threshold`); (iii) `CALL iceberg.system.rewrite_position_delete_files(table => ...)` run from Trino (Spark syntax — Trino uses ALTER TABLE EXECUTE; pasting Spark CALL into Trino fails with Procedure not registered); (iv) `EXECUTE compact_delete_files` (invented by analogy); (v) `SELECT FROM \"fct_events$delete_files\"` (no such metadata table — use `$files WHERE content = 1`); (vi) `SELECT FROM \"fct_events$position_deletes\"` (no such metadata table — same); (vii) `SET SESSION iceberg.merge_compaction_threshold = 100` (no such session property — invented from Spark/Iceberg config-style names); (viii) 'I'll fix this by running EXECUTE optimize from Trino more often — it'll clean up delete files too' (WRONG — Trino's optimize on 467 doesn't compact delete files); (ix) `incremental_strategy='upsert'` (no such dbt-trino strategy — valid values are append/delete+insert/merge per docs.getdbt.com); (x) 'Switch all tables to copy-on-write to fix the problem' (overcorrection — write amplification can be worse than original MoR slowdown); (xi) 'The fix is to drop and recreate the table' (loses snapshot history; last-resort blast radius).
